messages:
maria: Heads-up — we've got a strangely timed duplicate event showing up for a subset of streaming clients after the proxy half-closes the socket. Console telemetry shows a single server-side delivery but billing/ingest counters jump by +1 for the same request. Anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:

kai: Yep, saw early traces in the canary yesterday. It looks like the edge is flinging a final HTTP/1.1 RST or half-close and then the client reopens a new WS/SSE session. Downstream the runtime treats the resumed connection as a fresh request, so it double-bills.

jamie: Do we have any code-level evidence? logs or packet captures? If it's a half-close -> reconnect race we should be able to correlate connection ids.

maria: I pulled logs for one tenant: `conn=abc123` shows server delivered last chunk then closed normally. Console only prints one delivery. But billing ingestion shows `billing_event: req_id=xyz` recorded twice, timestamps 14s apart. There are matching client reconnects in the edge logs with `resume=false`.

kai: Edge snippet I grabbed: ```
[edge] client FIN -> proxy: half-close
[proxy] backend FIN -> client: keep-alive linger 0
[edge] proxy sends 499 then client retries over new socket
```
It smells like proxy translating half-close into an early termination signal to the client, which triggers client retry logic.

devex-ux: UX note — customers are seeing double tokens in the console graphs and assume duplicate model outputs. We should surface a distinct metric for "recovered-by-reconnect" vs "delivered-on-first-connection" so users can triage.

jamie: Two orthogonal fixes: (1) make billing ingestion idempotent by request fingerprint (req_id + connection_epoch) so retries don't double-bill, (2) make the runtime expose a short-lived ack that the server emitted final-event and the edge won't accept immediate retries for the same req_id. Which is easier?

kai: (1) is straightforward if we can derive a stable fingerprint — but many clients don't send a unique req_id on initial connect. We could synthesize from tenant+session+first-event-hash, but risk collisions. (2) requires protocol changes and coordination with multiple proxies.

maria: Another thought: add an opt-in header `X-Stream-Id` that clients can set; edge will pass it through and runtime will use it to dedupe billing. Short-term for the pilot. Longer-term, runtime-side dedupe with a TTL seems safer.

devops-bot: CI run for `edge-proxy` branch `fix/hs-retry-signal` completed: 14 tests failed (mostly around http2 stream reset semantics). Link: https://ci.internal/edge/9876 :warning:

jamie: Can we instrument the console to flag sessions where `edge_reconnects > 0 && server_deliveries == 1`? That would help ops triage without changing runtime.

maria: Good call. I'd also like a small trace span from edge->proxy->runtime in the request flow so we can visualize the exact sequence. We currently log them separately but not correlated.

kai: I'll prototype a probe that adds a `trace_id` to SSE `:comment` lines for the next canary. Example: `:trace=ti-9f4a`. It's low-impact for clients.

devex-ux: For the console change — suggest adding a per-session banner: "Potential replay detected — reconnect after half-close" with a link to a troubleshooting doc. That reduces support tickets.

jamie: Action items: (A) infra: add temporary billing dedupe window keyed on X-Stream-Id or synthesized fingerprint (kai +1), (B) console: add alerting/visual flag (devex-ux +1), (C) edge: add trace_id probe in canary (kai +1), (D) docs: triage steps for customers (maria +1).

maria: I'll draft the docs and open an RFC for a formal `stream-id` header. I'll also attach a sample `curl` SSE flow for support:```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "X-Stream-Id: s-987654" 
  "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/streams?model=gpt-lite"
```
If we recommend clients set `X-Stream-Id` it must be in public docs.

jamie: For the short term I'll push a billing rule: if an identical `X-Stream-Id` observed within 30s and the server logs show last-delivery < 5s before duplicate, mark the second as replay and don't bill. We'll need a migration plan to remove this hack once protocol dedupe exists.

kai: I'll start the canary with the trace probe at 03:00 UTC tonight. Expect noisy traces but we can filter.

devops-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: `edge-proxy` -> canary pool 5% at 03:00 UTC. Monitoring alert created (canary-keptalive-errors).

maria: Thanks. If folks see client-side recreation patterns please paste minimal client logs here. We want to be sure this isn't an app-level retry misconfigured for graceful shutdowns. :eyes:

jamie: Noted. I'll sync with support to capture a couple of repros and attach to the ticket.

kai: Also adding a small tutorial for partner integrators about how to set `Connection` semantics (`keep-alive` vs `close`) in common HTTP libs — will link it in the doc.

maria: Awesome. Closing loop: once we have canary traces and billing dedupe patch we'll validate with the tenant who reported the issue.

devex-ux: I'll add the console banner draft to the docs PR so we can ship both at once. :white_check_mark:
